# 4. Harness layer: how you run, test and trust it

[← Home](../README.md) · [The stack](README.md) · [Data layer](data.md) · [Agent layer](agent.md) · [Execution layer](execution.md) · **Harness layer** · [Application layer](application.md)

> **Is the result real, and would we notice if it stopped being real?**

**Scope.** Research and backtest environments, simulators and paper-trading gyms, benchmarks and live arenas, robustness and bias control, and the agent harness itself: loops, evals, traces and durable state.

**Where it usually breaks:** a test window the model has already read (look-ahead); headline Sharpe ratios from a few months; costs and slippage left out; regressions found in production instead of in a replayed trace.

**Open gap.** No catalogued agentic system's headline trading table can be regenerated from its repository. Live arenas fix look-ahead but run for weeks, far too short to separate skill from luck.

17 repos · 17 papers · 10 articles and posts. Legend: 🟢 active (last commit within 90 days of the check) · 🟡 slowing (within a year) · ⚪ dormant · ⚡ can place real orders · 📝 paper trading · 🧰 general-purpose tool applied here · 📖 read in full · 🗂️ machine-extracted [method card](../docs/cards/index.md) · 🔖 abstract only.

## Articles and posts

Newest first. Icons: 𝕏 post · 📝 blog · 📘 docs · 📰 news · 🎧 podcast · 📄 paper or report. A post is listed for the idea it carries; its own performance claims are not verified here.

- 📘 [Task verifiers](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/verifier) — Harbor Framework, 2026-10-26. How a container task's verifier runs after the agent finishes and writes a reward. A clean template for grading trading-agent tasks (build a backtest, reconcile a book) independently of the agent.
- 📘 [LangGraph persistence: checkpointers and stores](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/persistence) — LangChain, 2026-10-26. Thread checkpoints give resume, human-in-the-loop approval and time travel; stores give cross-run memory. TradingAgents and several projects here are built on LangGraph.
- 📘 [Strategies (Pine Script v6 user manual)](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/concepts/strategies/) — TradingView, 2026-10-26. The broker emulator's own realism caveats: intrabar paths inferred from OHLC unless the bar magnifier is on, unrealistic results on synthetic charts, and caps on bars and trades. Check these before trusting an agent-generated Pine backtest.
- 📝 [Building agents: When to fold subagents into your main agent loop](https://claude.com/resources/articles/building-agents-when-to-fold-subagents-into-your-main-agent-loop) — Diane Sarkis (Anthropic), 2026-10-22. Many agents do better as one loop with skills loaded on demand than as a coordinator with many subagents. Keep subagents for context isolation, parallel independent work or conflicting instructions, and migrate under evals. Directly relevant to analyst/risk/trader agent teams.
- 📝 [Pi Durable](https://earendil.com/posts/pi-durable/) — Earendil Engineering, 2026-10-01. Every step of an agent run is a checkpointed task, so a new process can resume after a crash. Read alongside the execution rule: replaying a step is not the same as knowing whether its order reached the broker.
- 📝 [Toward Recursive Self-Improvement: How GLM Built Its Own Inference Infrastructure](https://z.ai/blog/glm-built-its-inference-infrastructure) — Z.ai, 2026-09-17. A company's account of an infrastructure agent driven by dense, verifiable feedback, with objectives and risk kept by people. The lesson transfers: verifiable feedback loops, not credit for every gain to the agent. Claims are the company's own.
- 📄 [Dream-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Worlds](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14858) — Tong Zheng et al., 2026-09-14. Improves an agent's exploration policy offline by replaying its stored discovery history. An idea for budgeting strategy search; any trading use needs a held-out set that the improvement loop never sees.
- 📄 [Harness Engineering: Anatomy, Architecture, and Evolution of Coding Agents (a source-code study of eleven systems)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00006) — Paul Barbaste et al., 2026-07-15. Maps seven subsystems and 29 design patterns across eleven coding-agent harnesses. A vocabulary for the harness around a trading agent; it is a study of coding agents, not a capability table for trading.
- 📝 [Harness design for long-running application development](https://www.anthropic.com/research/harness-design-long-running-apps) — Prithvi Rajasekaran (Anthropic), 2026-03-24. Separate the generator from a skeptical evaluator, and revisit the harness with every new model to drop scaffolding it no longer needs. The case for an independent verifier, in practice.
- 📝 [Effective harnesses for long-running agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents) — Justin Young (Anthropic), 2025-11-26. An initializer agent sets up the scaffolding; a worker agent does one unit per session, tests end to end, and leaves git history and progress notes for the next session. The same pattern fits multi-day research and strategy builds.

## Builder notes

Recommendations from this list's maintainers, distilled from the sources above. They are design advice, not results reported by those sources.

- **Keep the verifier independent.** The component that grades a run must not share the agent's context or prompts. Fix the task, inputs, model and budget per experiment, turn every failed trace into a regression case, and keep a held-out set that no automatic improvement loop ever sees.
- **Write a run manifest for every backtest.** Record data snapshot, code commit, model and parameters, costs, and the in-sample and out-of-sample windows, and report results after costs. Use the [report card](../tools/evalkit/report_card.py) and the error bars in [reading a backtest](../docs/06-reading-a-backtest.md).
- **Prove a P&L with a ledger, not a screenshot.** A credible record shows when each input was available, the price it could have traded at, fees, realized and unrealized P&L, and drawdown. Screenshots of returns without an account ledger are marketing, however large the number.
